# RelaySwarm

Experimental peer-assisted HLS video delivery using WebRTC data channels and
Nostr relays for peer discovery and signalling. A separate native proof of
concept uses HyperDHT and Noise for installed Node applications.

**Status:** [v0.1.0 is the published GitHub prerelease](https://github.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/releases/tag/v0.1.0).
The 0.2.0 source candidate includes further production feature work; its
[delivery requirements](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/PRODUCTION-READINESS.md) remain open. MIT licensed,
Node 22.13+; CI uses Node 24. The npm registry is unpublished.

The [current experimental pilot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/STATUS.md#current-delivery-checkpoint)
runs exact `afbf052`. Nine required CI jobs, fresh 271-member package
consumption and guarded HTTPS deployment passed. The deployed TURN correction
reclaims expired or failed cache entries while preserving live leases and
unfinished work. Nostr and an authenticated host-supplied account API are
implemented; integrating websites supply their authentication.

The agreed feature surfaces are implemented, but production acceptance is
incomplete. The latest fourteen-context trial stopped during setup after
admission rate-limit responses and delayed control bodies. Its measured window
was zero; all owned cleanup passed. Explicit operator configuration for the
shared request budget passed local checks; deployment is pending. Matching capacity, two-hour/churn,
natural expiry, physical/browser breadth, difficult networks, measured wire/cost
benefit and immutable release/download acceptance remain open. v0.1.0 is the
published prerelease; 0.2.0 remains the source candidate. See the
[P01–P12 checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/PRODUCTION-READINESS.md#delivery-checklist).

[Documentation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/README.md) · [Installation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md) ·
[hls.js integration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/INTEGRATION.md) · [API reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/API.md) ·
[Evidence and remaining work](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/STATUS.md) · [FAQ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/FAQ.md) ·
[AI index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/llms.txt) · [Full AI context](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/llms-full.txt)

## Try it

Install ffmpeg with libx264 for synthetic media, then:

```sh
git clone --branch v0.1.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/forgesworn/relayswarm.git
cd relayswarm
npm ci
npm run demo
```

Open `http://localhost:8787`. The server generates two live H.264/AAC
renditions, keeps its publisher key in Node and signs commitments derived
from the local playlists. The player starts origin-only. Uploading requires
the viewer's explicit opt-in; controls include upload limits, quality
selection, an origin-only kill switch and a local JSON receipt download.

To use existing media:

```sh
npm run demo -- --media-dir /path/to/hls --manifest master.m3u8
```

See [the field-test guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/FIELD-TEST.md) for the supported HLS subset,
HTTPS access from separate devices and receipt interpretation. Synthetic
media requires ffmpeg; serving an existing directory does not.

The current source candidate includes a **broadcaster**: live
RTMP-to-HLS ingest, persistent publisher identity, cumulative viewer upload
allowances, measured peer choice and authenticated operator controls.
Optional RTMPS forwarding can send the source to an external platform
independently of RelaySwarm delivery. These features are absent from the
immutable v0.1.0 downloads. The [production feature guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/PRODUCTION-FEATURES.md)
also describes wider media, delegation, admission, durable budgets/reports and
native fallback. See [broadcasting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/BROADCASTING.md),
[operations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/OPERATIONS.md) and [container setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/deploy/README.md).

## Install the library

The release supplies an installable tarball, a standalone browser ESM bundle
and SHA-256 checksums:

```sh
npm install https://github.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/releases/download/v0.1.0/relayswarm-0.1.0.tgz
```

```js
import { createHlsSwarm } from 'relayswarm/hls-swarm';
import { createHlsPublisher } from 'relayswarm/hls-publisher'; // Node only
```

The host supplies hls.js. Install it separately for a host-page integration;
the source demo includes it as a runtime dependency. The release
bundle includes the browser loader's runtime dependencies. Pinned Git
installation and bundle usage are in [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md).

## What it does

| Path | Transfer and integrity | Signalling |
|---|---|---|
| Original CLI, `poc.mjs` | werift WebRTC; SHA-256 supplied by the sending peer detects transport corruption | Signed **plaintext SDP** on Nostr relays |
| Browser loader, `relayswarm/hls-swarm` | Native WebRTC; shadow compares with origin bytes, peer-first verifies stream-author-signed segment commitments | Pairwise NIP-44-encrypted signals, session wire version 3 |
| Native CLI, `native-poc.mjs` | HyperDHT/Noise; receiver enforces an independently expected digest and size | Pairwise NIP-44-encrypted one-shot dial authorisation, session wire version 3 |

The browser loader has three modes:

- **Off:** origin-only HLS, without swarm sockets, publications or peer connections.
- **Shadow:** origin bytes play as usual; sampled peer transfers measure
  potential delivery and add data traffic. Uploading defaults to off.
- **Peer-first:** a bounded peer attempt precedes the normal HTTP loader.
  Signatures, exact media context, size and SHA-256 must verify before bytes
  reach hls.js. Startup, thin buffers, missing peers and failed deadlines use
  origin. Benefits can differ substantially between viewers.

Peer-first requires a trusted signed kind-30311 stream event with the
experimental `["relayswarm", "redistribute", "1"]` tag and an expiring
commitment signed by that author or a host-trusted, author-scoped delegate.
Kinds 24170/24171/24172 and this authorisation tag are experimental assignments,
not an accepted RelaySwarm NIP or a stable interoperability guarantee.

## Why use Nostr for rendezvous?

Peers still need infrastructure to discover one another.
[P2P Media Loader uses WebTorrent-compatible trackers](https://github.com/Novage/p2p-media-loader/blob/main/FAQ.md#what-is-tracker).
RelaySwarm instead uses application-selected Nostr relays for presence and
signals, then sends media over the direct peer connection.

[NIP-53](https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/53.md) kind-30311
events can list relays. A host can reuse that selection, but this library does
not automatically read relay/STUN policy from them:
the host passes `streamEvent`, `swarmId`, `relays` and `iceServers` explicitly.
The HTTP origin remains responsible for initial media availability and fallback.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    O[HTTP origin and publisher]
    R[Application-selected Nostr relays]
    A[Viewer A]
    B[Viewer B]
    A -. presence and encrypted signals .-> R
    B -. presence and encrypted signals .-> R
    O -->|HLS and signed commitments| A
    O -->|HLS fallback| B
    A <-->|verified media over WebRTC| B
```

Other approaches and the narrow comparison are in [Landscape](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/LANDSCAPE.md).
[RelaySwarmKit](https://github.com/forgesworn/relayswarm-kit) is a separate Swift
signalling/transport project. Published Kit v0.5.0 supports session version 3
and signed media. Its public SDK received verified author/delegate HLS bytes
from the production browser loader and rejected corruption and revocation.
That measured macOS arm64/Chrome loopback journey and its boundaries are in the
[protocol draft](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/NIP-DRAFT.md); physical-device and NAT acceptance remain open.

## Evidence

The [release-main CI run](https://github.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/actions/runs/38233694634)
passed all seven standard jobs: the publisher/player playback regression,
shadow and peer-first Chrome harnesses, native tests on Linux/macOS/Windows,
and public-relay transport tests.

The [twelve-viewer loopback soak](https://github.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/actions/runs/38231951028/attempts/2)
used three arrival waves and a 180 s final measurement window. Peers supplied
923 of 1,343 fragment loads (68.7%); all twelve viewers and the baseline had
zero stalls or fatal errors. Corruption was rejected, sampled resources stayed
within limits and shutdown released resources. Two viewers used origin
throughout. Media loads avoided exclude signalling, commitments and protocol
overhead; they are not net connection-data savings.

The two-rendition playback regression covers quality switches, forward/backward
seeks, shared-file byte ranges, a timestamp reset, relay loss/recovery,
receive-only behaviour, the kill switch and downloaded receipts.
[Status](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/STATUS.md) separates this evidence from remaining field gates;
[spike results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/spikes/RESULTS.md) retain dated historical measurements.
Earlier CLI/browser and limited cross-NAT runs do not validate the new loader
on physical phones or a broad range of internet networks.

## Commands

| Command | Purpose and prerequisites |
|---|---|
| `npm run demo` | Publisher/player; ffmpeg for synthetic media |
| `npm run check` | JavaScript syntax |
| `npm run check:docs` | Documentation links, AI index structure and generated-context freshness |
| `npm run docs:generate` | Regenerate `llms-full.txt` from maintained Markdown |
| `npm run test:swarm` | Browser-loader and hardening unit tests |
| `npm run test:publisher` | Publisher context/range and demo HTTP/relay tests |
| `npm run broadcast:install` | Fetch the platform-pinned MediaMTX test router |
| `npm run broadcast` | Unreleased live ingest launcher; FFmpeg, H.264/AAC input |
| `npm run test:broadcast` | Real ingest/reconnect/forwarding plus control guards; FFmpeg/OpenSSL |
| `npm run test:broadcast:browser` | Real-time two-quality Chrome playback; installed router and FFmpeg |
| `npm run test:operator` | Actual Chrome allowance, remote policy and reporting controls |
| `npm run test:media-browser` | Actual fMP4/ABR, audio/AES/mixed-codec and low-latency-part Chrome journeys |
| `npm run native:fetch -- --help` | Installed native client with verified HTTP fallback |
| `npm run test:native` | Local relay and local HyperDHT bootstrap; no external network |
| `npm run test:playback` | Two-rendition real Chrome regression; Chrome and ffmpeg |
| `npm run test:playback:resume` | Trusted Resume click, decoded media and fresh consent; Chrome and ffmpeg |
| `npm run test:browser -- --mode shadow` | Live HLS Chrome harness; Chrome and ffmpeg |
| `npm run test:browser -- --mode peer-first` | Authenticated peer-first harness; Chrome and ffmpeg |
| `npm test` / `npm run poc` | Original WebRTC PoC/fan-out against public Nostr relays |
| `npm run poc:native` | Native PoC against public relays and DHT bootstrap nodes |
| `npm run audit` | Dependency audit at the high-severity threshold |

Use `--chrome /path/to/chrome` for either browser test, or set `CHROME_PATH`.
The optional twelve-viewer CI soak is enabled by a manual workflow dispatch
with `soak=true`. Public-relay failures can reflect relay policy or availability.

## Privacy and limits

Swarm keys are ephemeral and separate from social identities. Participation
is pseudonymous: relays see metadata and connecting addresses, and connected
peers can learn one another's network addresses. NIP-44 hides signal bodies,
not those observations. The original CLI still exposes its SDP to relays.
Origin-only mode avoids swarm participation; the origin still receives normal
HLS requests. Upload consent and publisher redistribution permission are
separate requirements.

The optional [shared upload allowance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/ACCOUNT-UPLOAD-BUDGET.md) uses
explicit Nostr sign-in or a host website account to coordinate media reservations
across devices. Its private service can associate those devices; linking both
identities also reveals their association to that service. Stable account
identities and grants stay out of swarm traffic and receipts. Sign-in never
enables uploading or reporting. The deployed `8f482b4` pilot offers Nostr sign-in;
integrating websites supply their own authenticated account resolver.

The browser defaults to Google's public STUN server unless the host supplies
`iceServers`; the native path uses HyperDHT bootstrap/routing nodes instead.
No managed TURN or super-peer service is supplied. Hosts can pass TURN ICE
credentials through `iceServers`. For browser HLS, blocking peers or
relays leaves the normal origin loader as fallback. The native CLI reports
failure; the installed native client adds verified HTTP fallback. The swarm provides neither durable
storage nor availability after every source disappears.

Still outstanding: physical-phone and varied-NAT trials, sustained operation,
broad internet scheduling/cost evidence, a full Sybil suite, an accepted NIP
and released independent-client interoperability. Actual fMP4/adaptive-quality
and wider-media fixtures are recorded separately from physical acceptance.
See [Threat model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/THREAT-MODEL.md) and [the field gates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/FIELD-TEST.md).

## Documentation and AI readers

The canonical public repository is
[`forgesworn/relayswarm`](https://github.com/forgesworn/relayswarm).

is a short index with direct Markdown links;
[`llms-full.txt`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/llms-full.txt)
is generated from the maintained guides. Published code is pinned at `v0.1.0`;
documentation on `main` can include later corrections. [Maintaining the docs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/MAINTAINING-DOCS.md)
explains regeneration and publication checks. The release assets remain v0.1.0
until a new release is actually published. [Changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/CHANGELOG.md) records
release and documentation changes.

# Integrating the hls.js swarm in a host page

[Documentation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/README.md) · [Installation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md) ·
[API reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/API.md) · [Release evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/STATUS.md)

`src/browser/hls-swarm.mjs` adds peer-assisted delivery to an hls.js player.
In **shadow mode** it changes nothing the viewer sees: every fragment still
comes from the origin, and the swarm only measures what peer delivery would
have achieved. That is the mode to deploy first.

The module is browser ESM with a direct runtime dependency on `nostr-tools`.
The published [v0.1.0 GitHub prerelease](https://github.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/releases/tag/v0.1.0)
supplies an installable tarball and a standalone bundle containing the browser
runtime dependencies. The host supplies hls.js. The npm registry is unpublished;
[Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md) gives exact asset and pinned-Git commands.
The current 0.2.0 source adds the
[production feature work](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/PRODUCTION-FEATURES.md); those additions are
absent from v0.1.0 assets and retain separate delivery/acceptance gates.

The host selects a trusted stream event, shared swarm id, relay policy and ICE
servers. This module does not perform Nostr stream discovery or automatically
extract relay/STUN policy from a kind-30311 event.

## Attaching

This host-page snippet assumes the application provides `eventId`,
`manifestUrl` and the `video` element. Replace the example relay with your own
tested endpoint. The metrics callback below logs locally; the library does not
submit analytics automatically.

```js
import Hls from "hls.js";
import { createHlsSwarm } from "relayswarm/hls-swarm";

const swarm = createHlsSwarm({
  swarmId: `stage-${eventId}`,        // same string for every viewer of one stream
  relays: ["wss://relay.example"],     // 1-8; the deployment's own relay first
  mode: "shadow",                      // "shadow" | "peer-first" | "off"
  originFallbackMs: 1500,              // "in time" means within this of the load starting
  shadowSampleRate: 0.25,              // race this share of fragments (see Cost)
  onMetrics: (metrics) => console.log(metrics),
});

const hls = new Hls();
swarm.attach(hls);                     // attach BEFORE loadSource
hls.loadSource(manifestUrl);
hls.attachMedia(video);

// later, or when the kill switch says off
swarm.stop();
```

An invalid supported configuration or unsupported browser yields a swarm
whose `metrics().mode` is `"off"` and whose `metrics().disabledReason` says
why (`invalid-swarm-id`, `invalid-relays`, `invalid-mode`, `mode-off`,
`invalid-stream-authorisation`, `missing-commitment-provider`, `invalid-limits`, `no-webcrypto`, `no-webrtc`, `no-websocket`). A
disabled swarm leaves the player untouched, so the host page can attach
unconditionally.

`attach()` replaces `hls.config.fLoader` with a wrapper around the loader that
was configured, and `stop()` puts the original back, closes every peer
connection and relay socket, drops held segments and emits one final
`onMetrics`. Requires a secure context (https, or localhost) for WebCrypto.

For a same-identity admission renewal, `updateTicket(ticket)` replaces only this
viewer's opaque ticket and schedules a bounded presence announcement. Established
links, the loader, held segments, counters and upload reservations remain intact.
It returns `true` for an accepted ticket (including an unchanged one), or `false`
for an invalid ticket or stopped, disabled or ungated swarm. The host must validate
its own credential's issuer, swarm, epoch and expiry before calling it, and retain
expiry checks around asynchronous admission and upload reservations. It does not
validate an opaque credential, extend policy authority or restore upload consent.
Publisher, policy or peer-configuration changes still require reconfiguration.

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `swarmId` | required | Groups viewers of one stream. 8-128 characters. |
| `relays` | required | 1-8 relay URLs (`wss://`, or `ws://` on loopback). |
| `mode` | `"shadow"` | `"off"` disables; `"peer-first"` requires a signed stream authorisation and commitment provider. |
| `secretKey` | fresh per viewer | Ephemeral signing key for presence and signalling. Never the viewer's own identity. |
| `originFallbackMs` | `1500` | The in-time budget a peer delivery is measured against. |
| `originReserveMs` | `2000` | Peer-first reserves this much buffered playback for the origin; an empty buffer goes directly to origin. |
| `lateWindowMs` | `6000` | How long a race keeps asking peers before it counts as missed. |
| `maxPeers` | `6` | Connections in and out. |
| `maxDialsInFlight` / `dialTimeoutMs` | `2` / `12000` | Simultaneous outbound dials and setup deadline. |
| `maxUploadPeers` | `4` | Distinct peers served in any 30 s. |
| `maxUploadBytesPerSecond` | `1250000` | Upload token bucket. |
| `maxUploadBytesPerSession` | unlimited | Optional non-negative safe integer, including zero. Reserves full accepted media payloads; interrupted transfers do not refund the allowance. |
| `reserveUploadBytes` | none | Optional async `(bytes, {signal}) => boolean` host reservation before serving; refusal/error/timeout stops the send. Use for persistent cross-tab budgets. |
| `serveOnCellular` | `false` | With `false`, detected cellular or `saveData` connections neither upload nor fetch peer media. Detection is advisory and does not identify every metered connection. |
| `serve` | `false` | Set `true` only after the viewer opts into uploading. With `false`, the viewer is receive-only: it takes from peers but never uploads or advertises what it holds. Use it where the connection type cannot be read (Safari), so a phone on cellular is never asked to upload. |
| `ticket` | none | An opaque string (up to 2 KB) this viewer presents in its presence and in every offer and answer, typically a short-lived credential the origin signed for this viewer's swarm key. |
| `admit` | none | `(pubkey, ticket) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>`. With it set, a viewer never dials, answers or follows a referral to a peer it has not admitted, so its address (carried in the SDP) only reaches ticket holders. The host is called again before each dial and SDP publication, including retries and referrals; it must check expiry. A third argument provides an operation-specific abort `signal`, cancelled on its deadline or swarm stop. At most 16 checks run concurrently and each has a 3 s deadline. |
| `shadowSampleRate` | `0.25` | Share of fragments raced. |
| `streamEvent` / `getCommitment` | required for peer-first | Signed kind-30311 stream event and `(context, { signal }) => signedCommitment`. See below. |
| `delegation` / `revokedDelegationIds` / `delegationRevocations` | none / empty | Explicit author-signed scope and current host revocation view for delegated commitments. |
| `maxConcurrentRaces` | `24` | Maximum retained shadow races. |
| `admissionTimeoutMs` | `3000` | Deadline for a host admission check. |
| `swarmParts` | `false` | Include low-latency HLS parts. Parts are small; leave off. |
| `maxHeldSegments` / `maxHeldBytes` | `12` / 64 MiB | What a viewer keeps to serve others. |
| `maxSegmentBytes` | 16 MiB | Maximum accepted/retained segment payload. |
| `minLinkLifeMs` / `idleEvictMs` / `evictionCooldownMs` | `15000` / `20000` / `10000` | Minimum link lifetime, bidirectional idle threshold and rotation cooldown. |
| `retryFloorMs` / `retryCeilingMs` / `maxRetriesPerPeer` | `4000` / `45000` / `3` | Refusal retry bounds and retry attempts per peer. |
| `maxReferrals` | `2` | Maximum referrals offered after a refusal. |
| `reannounceDebounceMs` / `minReannounceGapMs` | `4000` / `12000` | Bound capacity-change presence announcements. |
| `presenceIntervalMs` | `20000` | Presence heartbeat, jittered 30%. |
| `metricsIntervalMs` | `10000` | How often `onMetrics` fires. |
| `iceServers` | one public STUN | Host-provided STUN/TURN configuration captured at swarm creation. Browser TURN credentials are disclosed to the client; no managed TURN deployment is supplied. The demo/broadcaster accepts a private `--ice-config FILE` or a separate optional [renewal adapter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/FIELD-TEST.md#optional-turn-credential-renewal) that replaces demo swarms. |
| `iceTransportPolicy` | `"all"` | `"all"` or `"relay"`, captured at creation and passed to every native connection. `"relay"` restricts peer ICE to relayed candidates; it never retries with `"all"`. Usable TURN configuration is required for peer connectivity. This does not select TLS, change consent or extend a peer deadline; origin fallback remains available. |
| `segmentKey` | URL pathname | Maps a fragment URL to the key peers index by. Must agree across viewers, so strip per-viewer query strings and CDN tokens. |
| `RTCPeerConnectionImpl` / `WebSocketImpl` | globals | Injection points for tests. |

The pending glare-reuse correction keeps the existing lower-public-key offer
when both peers dial simultaneously. The yielding peer may adopt only its
still-pending outgoing connection for the winning admitted offer. Native
operations are serialised and old negotiation/channel callbacks are fenced;
the same capacity slot and original absolute `dialTimeoutMs` deadline remain.
The host admission check runs again before rollback, after asynchronous rollback
immediately before remote SDP, and before answer publication. These checks share
the existing dial deadline and bounded admission policy. Established, failed or
unsupported native states are not reused; failure retains normal origin fallback.
Recent admitted offer IDs are retained privately up to 256 entries per swarm;
active incoming duplicates do not allocate or restart a timer. Incoming distinct
requests still supersede pending incoming connections. Wire version, public
options and existing limits stay unchanged. The correction has passed 121 unit
tests; native rollback/SCTP and Internet renewal remain unproved. See the
[current checkpoint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/STATUS.md#current-delivery-checkpoint).

## Cost, and what to tell viewers

Shadow mode downloads a raced fragment **twice**: once from the origin for the
player, once from a peer to measure. That is the price of measuring with no
playback risk. Keep `shadowSampleRate` low enough that the extra data is
acceptable (0.25 gives a useful sample), and leave `serveOnCellular` false.
Contribution is off by default. Say plainly that `serve: true` redistributes
media, and obtain the viewer's opt-in before enabling it. Cellular detection
is advisory: browsers can omit connection information, so it cannot replace
consent. Receive-only still discovers peers and exposes its address to them;
`mode: "off"` or `stop()` provides origin-only playback.

## Metrics

`onMetrics(metrics)` and `metrics()` return a version-2 snapshot: `v`, `swarmId`,
`mode`, `disabledReason`, `stopped`, `pubkey` (the ephemeral swarm key,
not an identity), `uptimeMs`, `serving`, plus:

- `peers`: `connected`, `dialling`, `dialsStarted`, `dialsAccepted`,
  `dialsFailed`, `dialsTimedOut`, `dialsRejected`, `offersAccepted`,
  `offersRefused`, `linksOpened`, `linksClosed`, `banned`,
  `candidatePairs` (counts keyed `local/remote` candidate type, the NAT
  outcome: `host/host`, `srflx/srflx`, `relay/...`, `unknown`).
- `signalling`: `samples`, `medianMs`, `p90Ms` from offer sent to channel open.
- `segments`: `originLoaded`, `raced`, `noPeers`, `sampledOut`, `skipped`,
  `aborted`, `peerInTime`, `peerLate`, `peerMiss`, `peerCorrupt`,
  `peerUnverified`, `inTimeShare`, `sampledInTimeShare`, `observedInTimeShare`,
  `sampledInTimeByteShare`, `observedInTimeByteShare`, `peerFirstLoaded`,
  `originFallbacks`, `commitmentRequests`, `commitmentRejected`,
  `commitmentUnavailable`, `peerFirstShare`, `peerFirstByteShare`, `peerLatencyMedianMs`,
  `peerLatencyP90Ms`, `originLatencyMedianMs`.
- `bytes`: `fromOrigin`, `fromPeers`, `peerFirst`, `uploaded`, `uploadsServed`,
  `uploadsRefused`, `held`, `uploadRemaining` (null when unlimited),
  `uploadExhausted`.
- `peers.deliveryMeasurements`: bounded measurements for active links,
  including completion time, payload rate and failures.
- `relays`: `connected`, `presenceSent`, `signalsSent`, `published`,
  `rejected`, `publishErrors`.
- `errors`: `total` and `byStage`.
- `config`: the effective settings, so a receipt says what produced it.

Snapshots contain no IP addresses, user agent or long-term key, but the
ephemeral public key can correlate a receipt with public swarm activity.
Keep receipts local unless the viewer explicitly agrees to reporting. The
current demo's optional reporting endpoint accepts a numeric summary rather
than this full snapshot; see [operations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/OPERATIONS.md).

`peerEligibilityDiagnostics` is an additive local version-2 snapshot field in
the current source. Its fixed reason `counters` survive eviction from the
64-record ring; `capacity` and `dropped` describe that ring. Each row contains
elapsed `atMs`, numeric `cc` and `level` (null when unavailable), the already
computed initial `budgetMs`, `reason` and `matchingHave` (boolean or null).
`no-budget` records HAVE as **null/unobserved**: the loader does not compute a
segment key or inspect peer availability to populate this diagnostic. The
original origin fallback may still compute its normal key afterwards.
Positive-budget reasons distinguish `no-have-no-wait`, `no-have-wait`,
`wait-no-longer-eligible`, `wait-aborted`, `wait-expired`, `have-at-entry` and
`have-after-wait`; `aborted-before-eligibility` means cancellation after the
existing key computation, before the HAVE decision. Wait expiry/cancellation
also leaves HAVE null rather than claiming it was still absent. One load can
produce both a wait-entry and a wait-outcome row: counters count decisions,
not distinct segments. Budget is the initial allowance, not remaining request
time. Rows contain no segment keys, hashes, URLs, peer identities or addresses.
Each row also carries `budgetGeometry`: the calculation's final `currentTime`,
`bufferedEnd`, `playableEnd`, `fragmentStart` (seconds) and computed
`originReserveMs`. These are the values consumed by the original calculation,
without additional media or context getter reads. Finite signed values are
retained; unavailable or nonfinite values are null. The fixed `source` is
`buffer`, `no-media`, `no-buffer`, `error` or `unobserved`; `positionSource` is
`part`, `fragment` or null. Non-buffer sources leave the numeric fields null.
Wait outcomes retain their original geometry, rather than sampling the later
buffer. Each row and returned snapshot owns a copy. These values explain the
initial budget calculation, not donor availability or remaining request time.
They remain readable after stop and use the existing local/reporting-consent
boundary; they add no requests, authority checks or deadline changes. These
observations do not establish the cause of a failed peer transfer.

Deployed source `f393abf` includes `transportDiagnostics` within metrics version
2. It contains fixed-enum
`counters`, a ring of at most 64 `records`, `capacity` and an eviction `dropped`
count. Records contain a page-local, per-swarm numeric connection `id` (0 when
no PC is allocated/correlated), elapsed milliseconds in `atMs`, and fixed `event`/
`detail` values for gathering, native states, signalling stages and close reasons.
Unreadable native state uses the fixed `unknown` classification.
Local-description records may add `candidates` (count only, capped at 256) and
`candidatesCapped`; they contain no addresses, SDP, peer keys or request IDs.
`signal-send` means local signalling acceptance, not relay delivery or remote
receipt. The ring and counters remain readable after `stop()`; native listeners
are detached when their dial/link ends. No automatic reporting, signalling change
or connectivity fix is implied. Keep this diagnostic receipt local under the same
reporting-consent boundary as other metrics. The two ordinary cross-machine
short checks retained actual supersession, post-SDP dial timeout and established-
link request-timeout stages; their [public summary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/spikes/results/f393abf-ordinary-cross-machine-20261014.json)
is evidence of observation, not a connectivity repair. Numeric IDs do not identify
the remote role. Union sampled records by `(id, atMs, event, detail)` within each
swarm instance; never sum repeated ring snapshots as new events. A request-timeout
close identifies the branch, not the request start, available budget or reason
bytes missed it.

The pending correction adds fixed `negotiation` / `glare-yield` observations
for adoption of a pending outgoing connection. Its numeric connection ID remains
the same: this is neither a new native construction nor a completed link.
Superseded negotiation callbacks cannot label the adopted connection's later
description as an earlier offer. Existing close reasons and reporting consent
remain unchanged; this event does not prove successful native rollback or media.

`inTimeShare` remains conditional on having peers. `sampledInTimeShare`
includes sampled fragments with no peers; its byte equivalent weights by
fragment size. The `observed` shares divide verified in-time samples by all
origin-loaded fragments/bytes and are lower bounds when sampling is below 1.
Use sampled coverage alongside `noPeers` and `candidatePairs` when assessing
reachability. In peer-first mode, `bytes.peerFirst` counts verified bytes
actually delivered to hls.js instead of starting an origin fragment request;
`originFallbacks` counts loads delegated to the original loader. Shadow
coverage fields are null in peer-first mode.

`bytes.uploaded` counts payloads accepted for serving after the upload token
bucket, any host reservation callback, and the subsequent live-state checks.
Pending or refused host reservations never increment it. Session capacity is
reserved internally before awaiting that callback, so concurrent requests cannot
overspend; an accepted reservation remains charged if the link closes before
serving. Consequently `uploadRemaining` can include charges absent from
`uploaded`. An interrupted accepted transfer can send less than its counted
payload; signalling and protocol overhead are excluded. These counters are not
wire metering or acknowledged delivery, and durable host-ledger spend may exceed
accepted serving totals.

The session allowance is additive within metrics version 2. Exhaustion
withdraws media availability and stops serving while receiving remains
available. The library counts one swarm instance; a host recreating instances
must retain accepted totals. The demo uses an origin-wide Web Lock and
storage reservation across Apply, rejoin, publisher refresh, reloads and tabs.
Consent is never persisted. Storage failure disables uploading; an explicit
viewer reset or increase can change the quota.

Peer-first ranks eligible advertised media by measured completion time,
payload rate and failure history. Healthy measured peers take priority over
fast refusals; cold peers receive bounded exploration. A known delivery gets
headroom within the original peer deadline, rather than an equal share of it.
Attempts remain serial and capped by `maxPeers` and the original deadline.
A timed-out or cancelled request resolves promptly for origin fallback. On a
known ordered, fully reliable channel, the link stays busy while discarding
that response up to a matching validated EOF, or a refusal before metadata.
Only then can another request use the channel. The existing drain limit closes
an incomplete response; host stop and admission withdrawal close immediately.
Fresh-origin coordination is bounded by safe buffered playback and measured
HTTP fallback time. hls.js owns quality selection. These mechanisms do not
prove optimal internet scheduling or net savings.

## Authenticated peer-first loading

The runnable publisher/player example and the Node-only
`relayswarm/hls-publisher` helper are documented in
[`docs/FIELD-TEST.md`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/FIELD-TEST.md). The helper signs only contexts
present in its own local playlists, including exact byte ranges and
discontinuities; its supported HLS subset is deliberately limited.

```js
const swarm = createHlsSwarm({
  swarmId,
  relays,
  mode: "peer-first",
  streamEvent: signedLiveEvent,
  getCommitment: (context, { signal }) =>
    fetch(commitmentUrl(context), { signal }).then((response) => response.json()),
  serve: viewerHasOptedIntoUploading,
  originFallbackMs: 1500,
});
```

The host obtains a kind-30311 event from its trusted stream discovery flow.
The event must have a valid signature and the experimental tag
`["relayswarm", "redistribute", "1"]`. This opts the publisher into peer
redistribution. These assignments are a RelaySwarm contract, not an accepted
NIP or an interoperability claim.

The commitment is a Nostr event of experimental kind 24172, signed by the
same author or a trusted scoped delegate, tagged `x` with the swarm id and `e` with the exact stream event
id. Its content is the exact output of `commitmentContent(fields)` exported
by `relayswarm/segment-commitment`. Fixed field order and the
`relayswarm-segment-v1` domain bind the signature to this use:

```js
commitmentContent({
  streamEventId: signedLiveEvent.id,
  swarmId,
  key,                 // SHA-256 of swarmId + "\n" + segmentKey + byte range
  rendition: "0",      // String(context.frag.level)
  sequence: 123,       // context.frag.sn
  discontinuity: 0,    // context.frag.cc, default 0
  part: null,          // context.part.index, otherwise null
  sha256,              // digest of the exact media bytes
  size,                // exact byte count, within maxSegmentBytes
  expiresAt,           // Unix seconds, future and at most five minutes away
});
```

The default segment key is the URL pathname; a byte-range request adds
`#start-end`, matching the loader context. Publisher and viewer must agree
on this mapping. A commitment older than two minutes, a different stream,
rendition, discontinuity, sequence or part, an expired commitment, or a
signature from another key is rejected. Delegated commitment keys are not
implemented.

Signature validation, peer discovery, transfer and SHA-256 verification must
all finish within `originFallbackMs`. With a thin playback buffer the wait is
shortened to reserve `originReserveMs` for origin loading; startup, an
empty buffer or a fragment no peer advertises goes directly to origin.
Otherwise the original loader starts
and owns its usual HTTP retries and errors. Invalid peer bytes are discarded
and the peer is banned. Init segments and, by default, low-latency parts use
the original loader directly. `abort()`, `destroy()` and `stop()` cancel
pending peer work; stopping also immediately releases a waiting load to its
original loader. No late peer completion can invoke a second success callback.
Peer success updates the statistics object retained by hls.js, including loaded
bytes and timestamps. Aborting a pending peer load invokes `onAbort` once;
destroying it cancels without a completion callback. The playback regression
checks these behaviours alongside ranges, seeks and discontinuities.

## The kill switch

The host page owns the mode. Read it from your own stage status or config
(`off` / `shadow` / `peer-first`), create the swarm accordingly, and when a live change
flips it to `off`, call `stop()`. After `stop()` the player is exactly as it
would have been without the module, and a new swarm can be created later if
the switch flips back. Nothing in the module reaches back to the host to
decide its own mode.

## Known limits

- **Limited peer-first scheduling.** Each load asks one available peer at a
  time within a fixed deadline. Origin seeders can contribute substantially
  without receiving any peer-first segments themselves; per-viewer benefits
  are uneven. Fresh media coordination and measured deadlines are implemented;
  internet-scale scheduling, released independent-client interop and physical
  mobile/NAT measurements remain open. See the production delivery checklist.
- **Bounded peer resources.** A link queues at most four uploads, rejects
  empty or excessive chunks and has a 3 s backpressure deadline. These bounds
  limit particular attacks; they do not prove resistance to every Sybil or
  resource-exhaustion attack.
- **Rotation is narrow on purpose.** A peer at `maxPeers` rotates a link out
  only for a caller that has no peers at all, only when it would still keep one
  of its own, at most one per `evictionCooldownMs`, and never a link that is
  mid-transfer or younger than `minLinkLifeMs`. Rotating for anyone who asked
  was measured to cost late joiners more than it won, because an evicted peer
  re-dials at once and displaces a third. Other refusals carry a
  `retryAfterMs` and up to two referrals instead. `peers.evicted`,
  `peers.evictionsUnavailable`, `peers.retriesScheduled`,
  `peers.referralsFollowed`, `offersRefused` and `segments.noPeers` show what
  is happening, and `segments.firstPeerSegmentAtMs` says how long a viewer
  waited before the swarm was any use to it.
- **Hard NATs.** Symmetric NAT and some VPN egresses will not connect with
  STUN alone. A host can supply TURN credentials through `iceServers`; no
  managed TURN or super-peer service is supplied. When peer connection fails,
  viewers play from the origin.
- **Relays.** Presence is one event per viewer per 20 s plus two events per
  connection. Point at a relay you control; a public relay may rate-limit.
  Sessions subscribe to swarm-wide presence and only their own recipient-tagged
  signals. Relay frames must match a live subscription before signature work
  and dispatch; reconnect restores both subscriptions.

---

Source: [CHANGELOG.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/CHANGELOG.md)

# RelaySwarm changelog

## Unreleased

The 0.2.0 candidate remains unreleased pending final CI and acceptance.

- Expose the broadcaster's existing per-socket-address request allowance through
  `--admission-per-address-requests` (1–10,000, default 600). Other admission
  limits remain unchanged; field acceptance is separate.
- Reclaim settled TURN viewer entries after their credential cache expires or
  initial issuance fails. Fresh credentials and unresolved issuance keep their
  slots; the viewer, request, issuer and rate limits remain unchanged.
- Retain renewed admission tickets while peer retry or connection limits delay
  their next validation, without replacing a newer pending ticket when older
  work settles.
- Measure account authority against the signed issuer lifetime and conservative
  elapsed time, so small device/server clock differences do not reject a valid
  challenge. Keep the original grant/delegation limits, rollback revocation and
  server proof checks; issue all challenge timestamps from one clock sample.
- Add an explicit Resume playback action to rebuild suspended media from the
  origin, preserve errors/spend and require fresh Apply/upload consent before
  peer contribution. Explain disabled reporting when the server has it off.
- Retain an abandoned response on known ordered, reliable peer channels only
  until its validated response boundary or the existing drain timeout. Origin
  fallback stays prompt; late payload is discarded before connection reuse.
  Wire framing, playback deadlines and signed media verification are unchanged.
- Add redacted TURN lease provenance and conservative monotonic response timing
  for lifecycle measurement, retaining cached leases without moving their
  anchors. A passive debug getter exposes only epoch, ordinal and timestamp;
  it does not check or grant credential freshness.

- Add optional `issued`/`tls-tcp` TURN URL projection to the demo and broadcaster
  credential adapter. Explicit secure TCP is retained; only transport-unspecified
  secure URLs gain a TCP selection. Raw leases, expiry and upload consent remain
  bounded. This is configuration support, not selected-path or field proof.
- Add explicit `all`/`relay` ICE transport policy to the swarm, demo and
  broadcaster, defaulting to `all`. Relay-only does not force TLS or establish
  a delivery repair; changed demo policy requires fresh viewer Apply and consent.
- Refuse redundant stop IPC after a broadcaster worker's first force request
  or drain witness, preserving its original cleanup proof and deadlines.
- Expose the broadcaster's per-socket-address admission ticket limit through
  `--admission-per-address-tickets` (1–120, default 12), without changing other
  admission limits or establishing multi-viewer acceptance.
- Keep a live process-group wrapper for broadcaster worker shutdown, using its
  original private IPC channel instead of signalling a reaped leader's numeric
  PID. Preserve output, inner exit status and the existing dirty recovery fence.
- Added complete live-playlist blocking reload across compatible renditions,
  with bounded waits, disconnect/shutdown cleanup, directory replacement
  revalidation and snapshot-consistent HEAD/range responses.
- Filter unrelated named file events from playlist reload watches while retaining
  authorisation coverage, directory replacement checks and bounded revalidation.
- Reuse the pending browser connection when simultaneous offers require it to
  yield, with fresh admission checks, fenced callbacks and its original dial
  deadline. Native browser and Internet qualification remain separate gates.

- Added an optional durable account upload allowance supporting Nostr sign-in,
  host website accounts, explicit linking and short-lived page authority.
  Account actions preserve cumulative charges and require fresh upload consent.
- Added bounded numeric peer-eligibility observations to distinguish deadline
  and availability decisions without changing peer selection or its budgets.
  Records retain the original buffer geometry; the broadcast fixture observes
  existing request timings with explicit pending and missing measurements.
- Separated in-flight upload quota from accepted-upload metrics so a pending
  or refused host reservation cannot be archived as an uploaded payload.

- Added fresh live-media coordination, measured fallback reserves and actual
  fMP4/adaptive, audio, AES-128, mixed-codec and low-latency-part journeys.
- Added exact schema 2 media commitments, scoped signing delegation/revocation
  and linked signed NIP-53 advertisements without changing stable authorisation.
- Added bounded admission, persistent cross-tab upload budgets, idempotent
  durable reports and two-lease worker supervision with tested crash cleanup.
- Added an installed native client with verified HTTP fallback, acknowledged
  connection readiness and an absolute completion deadline. Native presence
  discovery accepts valid cached announcements without widening signal replay.
- Upgraded and published RelaySwarmKit v0.5.0; its public SDK passes author,
  delegate, corruption and revocation journeys against the actual browser sender.
- Added one bounded origin-only media repair, cancellation and timeout handling;
  fatal records and spent upload allowance remain in the receipt.
- Fixed Windows hash-cache deduplication, malformed relay-filter crashes,
  discovery eviction, worker descendant cleanup and pending-write queue bounds.
- Fixed expired host callbacks leaving HTTP requests outstanding, and added
  bounded native discovery when relays replay no ephemeral presence history.
- Reproduced and repaired a nonfatal live-playback stall after an interrupted
  quality switch and a new media continuity. A fresh live window and ten
  seconds without decoded-frame progress permit the existing single origin
  repair; cancellation, allowance usage and original errors remain preserved.
- Made playback checks prove each rendition's peer delivery before seeking,
  and added physical iPhone targeting and scoped Safari-window focus to the
  acceptance harness.
- Added bounded numeric control-request diagnostics, private STUN/TURN browser
  configuration and failed-TLS-startup cleanup.
- Fixed demo, broadcaster and probe commands silently doing nothing when
  launched through an absolute filesystem alias. Imports still leave their
  commands stopped.
- Fixed the single VOD repair repeating a video-only prefix after a later
  fragment introduced audio. It waits for media reattachment before resuming
  at the validated failing fragment; original errors and allowance remain.
- Made container public code readable and directories traversable when a build
  context uses private modes, while retaining private state permissions.

## 0.2.0 source candidate — broadcaster work on 12 October 2026

This source work has not yet been published as a release.
The earlier intermittent hosted MSE failure and physical-device, separate-network,
sustained-operation and external-platform acceptance remain open.

- Added a supervised H.264/AAC broadcast bridge with two HLS renditions,
  continuous sequence numbers, source recovery and independent RTMPS forwarding.
- Added private persistent publisher identity, bounded hash/signature caches,
  cumulative viewer media upload allowances and measured peer selection.
- Added authenticated operator status/policy and explicitly opted-in bounded
  numeric reporting; fixed cancelled HTTP media response cleanup.
- Added a host-scoped trusted Nostr stream adapter and an isolated container
  pilot package, with real transport/browser checks and documented acceptance gaps.
- Included the broadcaster/demo runtime dependencies in production installs and
  excluded local IDE metadata and private state from the package.
- Refreshed the documentation for the GitHub distribution and measured
  browser/native capabilities; separated planned work and historical observations.
- Added a documentation index, getting-started guide, module API reference and
  release evidence/status page.
- Reworked `llms.txt` with direct public Markdown links, added generated
  `llms-full.txt`, and added documentation freshness/link checks.
- Corrected RelaySwarmKit compatibility, phone validation, network-policy and
  measurement-cost claims; normalised repository metadata and discovery keywords.

## v0.1.0 — 12 October 2026

First [experimental GitHub release](https://github.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/releases/tag/v0.1.0),
commit `3e480e19dfe4d675f14bcb2968f3dc4926fbca25`.

- Original Nostr-signalled WebRTC CLI and separate native HyperDHT/Noise journey.
- Browser shadow and bounded peer-first HLS loading with author-signed commitments.
- Admission, connection/transfer bounds, consent defaults, rotation/referrals,
  lifecycle hardening and restored loader statistics/abort semantics.
- Local HLS publisher/player with exact-context signing, upload controls,
  origin-only kill switch, local receipts and controlled HTTPS trial configuration.
- Real Chrome regressions, native OS matrix, public-relay tests and an optional
  twelve-viewer soak; [evidence and remaining work](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/STATUS.md).
- Installable package tarball, standalone browser ESM bundle and checksums.

The npm registry remains unpublished. This release is a proof of concept.

# RelaySwarm documentation

RelaySwarm is an experimental peer-assisted HLS library and transfer proof of
concept. The [published v0.1.0 release](https://github.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/releases/tag/v0.1.0)
is separate from the current 0.2.0 source work on broadcaster and production features.
The repository and GitHub release are the public distribution surfaces; the
npm registry is unpublished. The operated
[HTTPS pilot](https://relayswarm.forgesworn.dev) is a controlled trial, with
its measured scope and acceptance gaps in [Status](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/STATUS.md).

| Task | Read |
|---|---|
| Understand the project and transport choices | [Project overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/README.md) |
| Install the package, browser bundle or source demo | [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md) |
| Attach the loader, configure consent/admission, read metrics | [hls.js integration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/INTEGRATION.md) |
| Find module exports and publisher/session methods | [API reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/API.md) |
| Review current production implementation and acceptance | [Production features](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/PRODUCTION-FEATURES.md), [delivery checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/PRODUCTION-READINESS.md) |
| Implement compatible session and commitment messages | [Protocol draft](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/NIP-DRAFT.md) |
| Run a trial on separate devices and interpret receipts | [Publisher/player field test](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/FIELD-TEST.md) |
| Ingest a live broadcast or add optional RTMPS forwarding | [Broadcasting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/BROADCASTING.md) |
| Operate private state, remote policy and opt-in reports | [Operations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/OPERATIONS.md) |
| Share an upload allowance across devices using Nostr or website accounts | [Shared upload allowance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/ACCOUNT-UPLOAD-BUDGET.md) |
| Deploy beside existing services with private ingest | [Container pilot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/deploy/README.md) |

For AI readers, start with the
[raw `llms.txt` index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/llms.txt).
The [generated full context](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/llms-full.txt)
collects maintained guides with absolute links. Historical spike code and
receipts remain separate so a dated experiment is not mistaken for current
